title: Assay-Verified Swarf Pooling for Machine Shops
one_liner: Turn the chip bin into a revenue line: two-bin alloy segregation, assayed weekly pickup, and pooled truckloads sold direct to mills and remelters.
customer: Ohio job shops and mid-size plants (20-300 employees) machining stainless, nickel alloys, titanium, brass or tool steel, especially aerospace, energy and medical suppliers. The first buyer is the plant manager or owner. A second buyer is any prime or OEM that wants a closed-loop 'revert' chain-of-custody.
problem: The chip bin is the only place in a shop where money leaves blind. Most shops tip all chips into one roll-off. The scrap yard grades by eye or its own XRF and pays a mixed-lot price. One shovel of aluminum in 316 stainless, or too much cutting oil, can drop the price by 30%-70%, while clean, segregated titanium and nickel-alloy turnings sell at multiples of mixed scrap. Nobody at the shop has time to sort, and small volumes are too tiny for mills to accept directly.
solution: 'SwarfStack': color-coded, RFID-tagged two- and three-bin systems in the shop, plus a weekly route truck with an onboard scale and a handheld XRF that assays each pickup and logs photo, weight, alloy and oil content to a shared ledger. A centrifuge or briquetter handles the oil. Pool by alloy across dozens of shops into full truckloads sold directly to mills, foundries and remelters. Pay the shop 70%-80% of net price and issue a digital scrap certificate for chain-of-custody. The provenance data becomes more valuable as metals tariffs increasingly reward proof of where metal was melted.
why_now: Reshoring is adding domestic machining hours, and with them chips. Metals lead times and alloy volatility keep prices high. The April 2026 Section 232 rewrite taxes the full customs value of metal derivatives and gives better treatment to U.S.-melted content, so provenance now has a price. Used handheld XRF analyzers now cost about what a used pickup does, and cheap vision models can identify alloy family from a photo of a bin.
revenue_model: A 20%-30% spread between the pooled sale price and what the shop is paid, plus $150-$300 per month bin and route fees, plus a small fee per digital scrap certificate. A route with 60 shops averaging $1,500 per month of chip value nets about $250k-$400k per year, before adding a briquetting and coolant-recovery arm.
non_obvious_insight: The scrap dealer's edge is not market power, it is that the shop does not know what is in its own bin. The metal was worth far more than the 'mixed' price, and shops give away five-figure sums each year without ever seeing the invoice line.
first_30_days: Buy a used handheld XRF for about $15k-$25k and rent a pickup with a platform scale. Sign 8 aerospace and medical suppliers in one county, starting with those cutting titanium, Inconel or stainless. Run pickups, assay each load, and send each shop a 'you left $X in your bin' statement showing the uplift against their current dealer. Pre-sell pooled loads to one stainless remelter and one titanium remelter before the first truckload.

title: Co-op Childcare Kits That Also Make Parent Friends
one_liner: Modern rails (licensing map, insurance, shift scheduling, lead-teacher placement) that let 12-20 neighbor families launch a parent-participation preschool or aftercare co-op in a few months, cutting tuition and curing parent isolation at the same time.
customer: Groups of 10-20 families in childcare deserts: new-parent groups, neighborhood and church parent groups, remote-work households, employer resource groups. Later: employers and HOAs that sponsor co-ops.
problem: Childcare averages $13,128 a year and the labor inside that price is the reason. Parents are lonely (friendship is now a measured health metric), and post-2020 new parents often have few local friends. Parent co-ops once made childcare 30-50% cheaper, but they withered because launching one requires legal, licensing, insurance and payroll expertise that volunteer boards lack.
solution: 'Co-op OS': a state-by-state navigator showing where parent-participation programs are exempt or lightly licensed (verify per state), template bylaws, an insurance bundle (general liability plus abuse-and-molestation), background checks and mandated-reporter training, a shift scheduler that assigns parent duty days and keeps a credit ledger, payroll for one paid lead teacher, and a lead-teacher matching service for displaced educators. Friendship is designed in: monthly parent-only dinners, a crisis buddy system and meal trains.
why_now: Dependent-care FSAs now reach $7,500 and the 45F credit lets sponsoring employers offset 40-50% of childcare costs. Hybrid schedules and AI-driven job churn have left many parents with flexible hours to trade for tuition. Parents are already organizing collectively on phones and schools, so collective action is normalized.
revenue_model: About $1,500 setup, $149/mo per co-op for software and payroll, insurance commissions, a lead-teacher placement fee of about $2,000, and employer sponsorship of co-op slots.
non_obvious_insight: Time is the new money. Childcare is expensive because it is labor, and co-ops swap parent hours for tuition. Nobody does it because of coordination and compliance, not desire. Parent friendship is the retention engine, not a nice-to-have, and lonely parents recruit each other for you.
first_30_days: Pick two states with clear parent-participation rules. Recruit 3 existing neighbor or parent Facebook groups into a 4-week 'Co-op Launch Sprint' with a $299 deposit per family. Engage an early-childhood attorney for templates and an insurance MGA for the bundle. Place one lead teacher and aim to have three co-ops running by January 2027.

title: Ex-Botter Red Team for Limited Drops
one_liner: Pay former sneaker-bot users to attack your product drop before launch, then rent you the checkout filter that stops what they found.
customer: Indie brands that run limited drops on Shopify with 500 to 5,000 units: streetwear labels, collectible toy and art-toy makers, TCG shops, sneaker boutiques, merch stores, small beauty and food brands. They pay $750 to $2,500 per pentest, then a per-drop or monthly fee.
problem: Brands think a waiting room or Cloudflare stops scalpers. It only stops speed. Real resellers win by multiplying identities, not by being fast. They use Gmail dot and plus tricks and catch-all domains, address jigging (Apt vs Unit vs #, an extra letter in the street name), virtual cards from one issuer, and residential proxies. One 'customer' becomes 40 orders. Fans get nothing, the brand gets angry DMs, and the resale premium goes to strangers. Small brands cannot afford enterprise bot vendors and do not know what to look for.
solution: Wedge: a 'Drop Pentest'. We run a real reseller stack against the brand's store or staging a week before launch and hand back a report: 'we would have captured 38% of your units, here is how'. Product: a Shopify checkout app called One Per Human. It normalizes emails, fuzzy-dedupes addresses (USPS-style standardization plus apartment and unit variants), clusters card fingerprints and BINs, phone-verifies and blocks VoIP numbers, and flags or auto-cancels suspected multiples before fulfillment, with a human review queue. Optional 'verified reseller tier' at a higher price so the brand captures some of the flip premium legitimately.
why_now: Collectible drops have become a public mess in 2025-26: Labubu and other Pop Mart drops, and Pokemon TCG releases where stores had fights, lines, and pulled product. Indie brands now copy sneaker-style drops, with sneaker-style bot pressure. Cheap LLM fuzzy matching makes address and identity dedupe far cheaper to build than it was two years ago. Shopify's checkout extensibility gives apps a place to validate or flag orders.
revenue_model: Pentest at $750 to $2,500. Guard app at $149 to $499 per drop, or 0.5% to 1% of drop GMV. Annual contracts for brands that drop monthly.
non_obvious_insight: Bots do not beat drops on speed. They beat them on identity multiplication, and the tells sit in the order data (address shape, email pattern, card issuer clusters) that the brand already has. Only someone who has run the tricks knows which tells matter. The poacher-turned-gamekeeper credibility is the moat, and the pentest report sells the product by showing the brand its own leak.
first_30_days: Days 1 to 7: build the attack checklist from what I and my Discord friends already do. Days 7 to 14: DM 100 small Shopify brands with an upcoming drop on Instagram, offering a free mini-audit built from their public store, such as how easy it is to create fake variants of an address. Days 14 to 30: convert 3 to 5 into paid pentests at $750 and use the findings to pre-sell the app. Delivery is mostly a spreadsheet plus screenshots.

title: Flat-Fee Guarantee Against Runaway Agent Bills
one_liner: Pay a few percent on top of model spend and the guarantee absorbs any overnight blowout above a hard multiple of baseline, enforced by an inline kill switch.
customer: AI-native startups and agencies spending $5k-$200k per month on model and tool calls (seed to Series B), including dev shops deploying agents for clients.
problem: Retry loops turn $0.40 tasks into $40, and five-figure overnight bills are reported. Blended token prices fell about 67% in a year but agentic workflows burn 5-30x more tokens, and 73% of enterprises overran AI budgets. The market sells dashboards and caps. Nobody sells a promise, and founders and their investors want the tail risk gone.
solution: A drop-in proxy (change one base URL) that sees all model and tool traffic and learns a rolling baseline per agent and workflow. The guarantee covers spend above a set multiple of baseline in a rolling window (for example 4x over 6 hours), up to a cap, paid as cash or credits. The proxy enforces circuit breakers so maximum loss is bounded, which makes underwriting tractable. Coverage applies only where default breaker policies were accepted, which controls moral hazard.
why_now: TechCrunch was covering the scramble over runaway AI costs by June 2026. Gateways are being absorbed into security suites (Palo Alto bought Portkey), and dozens of cap-and-alert tools have commoditized enforcement without offering a guarantee.
revenue_model: 3-6% premium on metered spend plus a gateway subscription, with parametric or MGA reinsurance for large limits.
non_obvious_insight: Whoever owns the kill switch can price the tail. A capped, enforced exposure is a parametric insurance product, not an open-ended liability. Buyers are paying for certainty, and the tooling is only how you deliver it.
first_30_days: Ship an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible proxy with breakers. Sign 10 startups to a beta guarantee capped at about $2k per incident, backed by a roughly $20k reserve. Price at about 4% of spend and log every incident. Talk to two parametric or MGA capacity providers.

title: Revenue Recovery From Blocked Shopping Agents
one_liner: Synthetic agent shoppers try to buy from your store every night, find where bot defenses and checkout kill legitimate agent orders, and you pay a cut of the sales recovered.
customer: Mid-market e-commerce merchants ($5M-$200M GMV) on Shopify Plus, BigCommerce or Adobe Commerce with aggressive bot, WAF and fraud settings, reached through their agencies and fraud vendors.
problem: Insiders think the bottleneck is protocol adoption (ACP vs UCP vs AP2). The measurable leak is simpler. Agent usage is about 62% at comparison but only about 23% at checkout. Fraud and bot systems built for humans misclassify agent traffic (Chargebacks911 warns of a false-decline problem). CAPTCHAs, SMS one-time codes and 3DS challenges kill legitimate agent orders, and the lost sale looks like a bounce, so no dashboard shows it.
solution: Run real agent stacks (ChatGPT agent mode, Comet, Gemini, open-source browser agents, plus ACP/UCP/AP2 clients) through scripted purchase journeys on the live store with test cards. Log the exact failure point: challenge page, WAF rule, OTP step, stale feed, price mismatch. Deliver a weekly fix list (allowlist verified agent signatures, rule changes, checkout patches), then re-test to prove recovery.
why_now: Bots now outnumber humans. Stores that blocked AI bots in 2024 are undoing it, and the Ninth Circuit ruling makes user-directed agents legitimate visitors. Five competing checkout protocols make failure modes hard to see.
revenue_model: $2-5k fixed audit plus 5-10% of attributable recovered agent revenue for 12 months, or $500-$2k/month monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: A performance-fee audit is easy to buy because the merchant risks nothing. The proof is measurable (before and after test purchases), and the data becomes a benchmark of which defenses block which agents.
first_30_days: Build the harness with 3 agent stacks and 5 common checkout and WAF patterns. Offer 10 free audits to Shopify agencies who can resell. Convert the first 3 leaks worth over $5k per month into revenue-share contracts.

title: Yield Twins and Robotic Cells for Regional Beef Packers
one_liner: Start with 3D vision yield scoring on the fabrication line and grow into robotic trimming cells for independent packers.
customer: Independent regional beef packers processing under about 2,000 head a day.
problem: Record cattle prices and a 75-year-low herd squeeze packer margins, while skilled knife labor is scarce and immigration enforcement hits meatpacking labor hardest.
solution: A camera-based yield-and-trim-loss scoring system for cut optimization, then robotic primal trimming and portioning cells sold as a service.
why_now: Physical-AI and 3D-vision costs dropped in 2025-26, and thin packer margins make a 1% yield gain worth millions.
revenue_model: Software at $2-4k per month per line first, then per-head fees for robotic cells.
non_obvious_insight: With margins this thin, the software yield gain pays before any robot works, and the data it collects trains the robot.
first_30_days: Visit three independent packers, mount cameras on a fab line, and deliver a first weekly yield report as a paid pilot.

title: Cloud-Bricking Escrow for Hardware Brands
one_liner: A neutral escrow-and-standby service that holds a hardware brand's cloud backend and local-mode firmware, and takes over the moment the cloud vendor fails.
customer: Consumer-hardware brands that outsource their cloud or app to an ODM or startup: private-label and licensed smart-home, router, EV-charger, pet-tech and e-bike brands. Retailers and insurers are secondary buyers.
problem: When a small backend vendor dies, the brand that sold the device takes the blame. Motorola-branded routers stopped being manageable when the MotoSync+ app failed. Play Store reviews say a third-party backend host's licence expired and the host ended operations ('Server Licence Expired'). Users report months without a fix. Spotify Car Thing became 'a $200 hardware turned into e-waste overnight.' An HN commenter estimated $300k-600k to open-source a single project, so afterthought rescue is unaffordable.
solution: For a flat annual fee, the brand deposits its backend container images and infrastructure-as-code, sealed secrets, signed 'local mode' firmware or companion-app builds, and device protocol docs. The operator monitors cloud health, domain and cert expiry, app-store status and vendor solvency signals. On a trigger it either runs the backend on standby infrastructure (pay-per-device) or releases the local-mode build. Brands that certify get an 'Afterlife Ready' mark for retail listings and regulator conversations.
why_now: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations began on 11 Sept 2026, with full manufacturer obligations from 11 Dec 2027 and lifecycle handling required. Startup shutdowns are running at a high rate: 14.4% of H1 2026 shutdowns were AI companies with a median age of 2.3 years and a median $30k cash at closure. Recent bricking cases (Motorola routers in Jun 2026, Nest thermostats, Kodak Pulse frames, Samsung fridges in Sept 2026) are fresh in retailers' minds.
revenue_model: $5-25k/yr escrow subscription per brand, plus $0.10-0.50/device/month for hot standby and a per-incident recovery fee. Certification audits are a later add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The liability chain runs from a dead vendor through the brand to the customer, and existing escrow (software licence escrow, to my knowledge) is not built for live device fleets. Evidence: the Motorola router thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48425611, 238 points) traces the outage to a third-party server licence expiring after the host company ended operations. The 'when hardware goes EOL' essay (https://www.marcia.no/words/eol; HN discussion at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46609492, 403 points) lists Nest, Car Thing and Kodak Pulse. It quotes the $300k-600k open-sourcing estimate and community workarounds (OpenWRT, 'No Longer Evil'). The EU CRA page (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act) sets the 11 Sept 2026 and 11 Dec 2027 dates. The buyer is the brand, not the consumer, and the fee has to be cheaper than a single recall.
first_30_days: Week 1: build a free 'BackendWatch' monitor that pings a brand's cloud endpoints, cert expiry and domain renewals. Week 2: cold-email 50 licensed-brand and private-label hardware companies, and Kickstarter-scale hardware founders. Weeks 3-4: sign 3 design partners on a $2.5k pilot escrow. Write the trigger contract with a startup-insolvency lawyer.

title: Turn Gray-Market Retatrutide Demand Into Trial Enrollment
one_liner: Intercept people searching to buy unapproved obesity drugs and route them, screened, to active trials that pay by the qualified referral.
customer: CROs, sponsors and trial sites running obesity and metabolic trials (paying per qualified lead or randomized patient), with the consumer as the traffic source.
problem: Sponsors struggle to recruit GLP-1-naive participants because prior GLP-1 use is an exclusion criterion and 22% of households already have a user. Meanwhile, non-trial retatrutide use grew ~1.8x per quarter, 71% of traced users bought outside trials, and Australia issued a liver and kidney injury alert in Jun 2026.
solution: A compliance-reviewed 'legitimate access' site and search and social funnel that meets intent ('retatrutide', 'triple agonist'), explains the risks, pre-screens (BMI, comorbidities, naive or washout status, geography) and refers to nearby enrolling Phase 2/3 sites. It screens out people who already took unapproved product where the protocol excludes them, and sponsors pay on qualified referral or randomization.
why_now: Retatrutide's Phase 3 program and Lilly's planned Q1 2027 filing are peak-hype. FDA and Lilly takedowns (>14,000 listings) push searchers toward risk. Pills at $149 are draining the classic trial pool, so recruitment cost per patient is rising.
revenue_model: Est. $150-500 per qualified referral and $2-6k per randomized patient, paid by CROs and sites, with performance tiers.
non_obvious_insight: Enforcement cannot remove demand. The highest-intent audience in obesity pharmacology is currently monetized by gray-market vendors, while trial sponsors pay per head for exactly the same people.
first_30_days: Build three landing pages and a screener reviewed by a regulatory consultant. Register with 3-5 enrolling sites and one CRO recruiter. Spend ~$3k on search and social ads for 'retatrutide clinical trial' style queries (check ad-policy limits) and deliver the first 50 pre-screened leads on a pay-per-qualified-referral contract.

title: Trusted Firmware for Chinese-Made Robots
one_liner: A security-audited, network-isolated software and attestation layer that lets US labs, utilities and cities legally buy and run cheap Unitree-class robots.
customer: US universities and research labs, utilities, municipal fleets, critical-infrastructure operators, and integrators reselling Chinese quadrupeds and humanoids.
problem: Chinese makers hold 86% of humanoid shipments and their robots cost a fraction of US alternatives, but security teams block procurement over cloud telemetry, remote access and radio vulnerabilities disclosed in 2025. There is no neutral, certified 'clean' stack, and barriers are going up.
solution: A replacement software stack and wrapper: local-only operation, cloud services removed, wireless interfaces locked down, signed OTA updates under customer keys, an SBOM, and a continuous-audit attestation report that security auditors accept. Add an optional network-quarantine gateway appliance.
why_now: Tariffs, the FCC's DJI action and expected legislation are tightening. Unitree's IPO signals the supply will keep coming, so buyers with budgets are stuck between the price advantage and compliance.
revenue_model: $500-1,500 per robot a year for the license and updates, $10-30k per security assessment, and about $800 per gateway appliance.
non_obvious_insight: Each time the US restricts a Chinese hardware category, a trust layer becomes the only route for legal buyers. Everyone bets on which hardware wins, but the money sits in the compliance gap. Risk: an outright ban would kill the market, so design for a pivot to open-source or allied hardware.
first_30_days: Buy a Go2 and a G1, reproduce the publicly documented vulnerabilities, and publish a hardening guide. Offer free audits to 5 university robotics labs' IT security officers and convert 3 to paid assessments at $10-15k.

title: Regrade: Stamped Reclaimed Framing Lumber
one_liner: A mobile lumber re-grading and code-acceptance service that turns torn-out framing lumber from chip-pile waste into stamped, sellable studs and joists for ADUs, garages and additions.
customer: Deconstruction and demolition contractors and salvage yards (pay per board foot graded, or sell us stock). Small builders, ADU builders and remodelers buy packages.
problem: Framing costs are climbing (Austin framing up 25-50%, adding $2-5K per home, and builders estimate tariffs at about $10,900 per home). A 44-year median housing stock throws off tons of dimensional lumber, but yards cannot sell it for structural use because building officials want a grade stamp, so most of it is chipped for fuel or mulch at tens of dollars a ton.
solution: A truck-mounted setup with a certified grader, de-nailer and moisture scanner, working with an accredited grading agency or agency-approved third-party graders to re-grade and stamp. It also produces acceptance packets for local building departments. Sell 'ADU framing kits' and pre-nailed wall panels made from stamped reclaimed lumber at 20-35% below new.
why_now: Tariff-inflated lumber and a July 2026 ROAD to Housing Act that streamlines review for multifamily of 15 units or fewer and funds standard duplex/townhome plans should create a wave of small infill and ADU projects. Framing-crew scarcity also favors pre-made panels.
revenue_model: Grading fee per thousand board feet; margin on framing kits and panels; salvage purchases from deconstruction crews.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier to reuse is paper, not supply. Old true-dimension, slow-grown lumber often grades at or above new stock, and small builders' need for speed means the buyer will pay for panelization.
first_30_days: Confirm with an accredited grading agency and two local building departments what re-grade stamps and packets they accept. Hire a certified grader by the day. Contract 3 deconstruction crews for lumber. Sell one ADU frame or garage kit to prove code acceptance and margins.

title: Insurer-Backed Self-Certified Permits for ADUs
one_liner: Japan-style private building confirmation: AI code review plus a licensed private reviewer plus an insurer-backed compliance warranty, so an ADU or small addition gets a certified package in about 48 hours where state law allows private providers.
customer: ADU builders, residential designers and architects, and homeowners in states with private-provider or third-party review statutes (Florida first), later cities piloting insured expedited review.
problem: Honolulu residential permits average 218 days (commercial 469). Government AI tools serve reviewers, and applicant-side tools for ADU owners, small builders and rural jurisdictions are thin. Faster review even increases filings (+34%) faster than permits issued (+5%).
solution: An applicant-side pre-clearance engine reads the plan set, runs the jurisdiction's zoning, structural and energy rules, and returns a correction list in minutes. A licensed private provider signs, and a surplus-lines policy from an MGA indemnifies owner and jurisdiction against code errors, priced from the engine's error data. Where private-provider laws exist the package is submitted directly, and elsewhere it is offered as an insured fast-track pilot.
why_now: Government pilots prove review can be automated (Honolulu review cycles down 58%, Denver's $4.6M contract). LLMs can now read plan sets. The ROAD Act funds standard blueprints. Insurers are hunting for new specialty lines, and applicants are desperate.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,000 per ADU permit package. 10-15% share of warranty premium. SaaS for designers.
non_obvious_insight: Governments will never build the applicant-side tool because of conflict of interest, but insurance can do what regulators cannot: price and carry the residual risk that a bad plan slips through. Japan has let designated private bodies issue building confirmations since the late 1990s, and permit timelines there are days, not months.
first_30_days: Partner with a Florida private-provider firm. Run 20 ADU and remodel plan sets free for three designers and compare predicted corrections to actual city comments. Pre-sell to ADU builders at $1,500 and show the accuracy data to two MGAs.

title: Widow-First Retention Drills for Wealth Advisors
one_liner: Sell independent advisors an annual 'if one of us dies' rehearsal for couples, because the defection risk sits at the first spouse's death, not with the kids.
customer: Independent RIAs and small wealth teams ($150M-$2B AUM) whose median client is 65+. The buyer is the firm principal or COO.
problem: The industry spends on next-gen events with heirs. Cerulli says about $54T of the transfer is spousal and about $40T of that goes to widowed women. The survivor is grieving, holds a house full of logins and unknown accounts, and has to decide whether to keep the advisor. Advisors are commonly said to lose most widows within a year (widely cited, verify). The cause is usually friction, not performance.
solution: A 90-minute 'Survivor Fire Drill' run by the advisor's team with a software kit. Each spouse's death is simulated in turn. The tool builds a First-90-Days playbook: who to call, which accounts exist, which autopays must keep running, and where the documents are. It audits titling and beneficiaries from the survivor's point of view and flags single points of failure, such as only one spouse knowing the passwords. It then schedules pre-agreed advisor check-ins at day 3, 14, 45 and 90. The advisor gets a dashboard of which couples have done the drill and where their exposure is.
why_now: Cerulli's Sept 2026 work frames retention of the transfer as the priority, and 89% of surveyed firms call family meetings essential. Wealth managers are buying heir-engagement tools, yet the first wave of money is spousal and the widow is under-served. Cheap document ingestion and secure vaults make the kit affordable for small firms.
revenue_model: $300-$700 per household per year billed to the firm, or a $25-40K/yr platform fee for a 100-household book. The ROI pitch: keeping one $1.5M widow at a 1% fee is worth $15K a year.
non_obvious_insight: The heir-retention narrative aims at the wrong person on the wrong day. Widows rarely leave over portfolio returns. They leave because nobody made the first 90 days easy. A rehearsal also works where estate planning fails, because people avoid 'planning' but will attend a scheduled drill.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 RIAs through advisor communities and podcasts. Run drills by hand with a spreadsheet and printed binder for each firm's 10 oldest couples. Record time-to-locate-accounts and the number of single-point-of-failure findings. Charge a $2.5K pilot fee and turn the findings into a retention case study the advisor can show prospects.

title: CJIS 6.0 Identity Kit for Small Agencies
one_liner: A managed multifactor and identity-verification stack that works in patrol cars, radio dead zones and shared workstations, ready for the Oct 1, 2027 CJIS deadline.
customer: Sheriff's offices and police departments with 10-150 sworn officers and no dedicated IT security staff, plus the managed service providers that serve them.
problem: CJIS 6.0 requires MFA and identity verification by Oct 1, 2027. Generic MFA breaks on shared terminals, offline vehicles and old mobile data computers. Small agencies buy compliance piecemeal from a few vendors and fail audits.
solution: Hardware keys plus a cached-token offline mode and a shared-workstation login flow, with an agency-level compliance dashboard and audit-ready evidence. Onboard officers in minutes through mobile driver's license or badge-based identity proofing.
why_now: The deadline is fixed and less than 13 months out. Agencies are starting budget cycles now, and state CJIS systems agencies will begin enforcing.
revenue_model: $8-15 per user per month or a per-agency package of $6-30K per year, plus hardware sold at cost plus margin.
non_obvious_insight: The real customer is the MSP serving 50 small agencies. One channel partner delivers dozens of deployments, and offline behavior is the differentiator that enterprise identity vendors will not build.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 MSPs that serve sheriffs. Prototype offline token caching on a rugged laptop. Run 3 no-cost pilots in agencies with upcoming CJIS audits.

title: Buy the Restaurant Alley: Used-Oil Route Roll-Up
one_liner: Consolidate small used-cooking-oil haulers into one AI-run route business, then sell every other mandated back-of-restaurant service from the same truck.
customer: Independent restaurants and small chains (who now get paid for their oil and buy add-on services), renewable diesel and SAF refiners buying traceable domestic feedstock, and retiring collector owners selling their routes.
problem: From 2026 the 45Z clean-fuel credit applies only to North American feedstock, and UCO prices have run at roughly $1,000 to $1,400 per tonne. Restaurants historically gave oil away under auto-renewing contracts with big renderers, and theft is common. Small collectors lack chain-of-custody paperwork and contamination grading, and refiners want traceable domestic supply.
solution: Acquire 8 to 15 small collectors, grease-trap pumpers and hood cleaners in one metro. AI ops: fill-level sensors or photo estimates to cut truck miles 25% to 40%, vision-based contamination grading at pickup, automatic chain-of-custody and sustainability documentation for refiners, and a contract-reading agent that finds competitors' termination windows and times win-back offers. Add hood cleaning, grease-trap pumping and fire-suppression inspection on the same route visits.
why_now: 45Z limits credits to North American feedstock from 2026, which makes domestic UCO scarce and valuable, and documentation that used to be optional is now a selling point. Owners of small routes are aging out, and route-optimization and photo-grading tools are cheap.
revenue_model: Spread on oil resale to refiners with a share paid to restaurants, plus $150 to $500 per add-on service visit, plus a traceability premium from refiners.
non_obvious_insight: The real asset isn't the trucks; it's the contract calendar. Thousands of evergreen grease agreements with 30 to 90 day cancellation windows can be read, mapped and timed. The alley visit is also the cheapest customer touchpoint for every other mandated back-of-house service.
first_30_days: Approach a retiring one-truck collector about a seller-financed purchase in the $200k to $600k range, or start as a broker with a subcontracted truck offering 20 to 30 restaurants a paid pickup. Build a photo-based intake and contract tracker. Target franchisee groups with 5 to 10 units. Pre-sell forward oil volume to a regional biodiesel or renewable diesel refiner using documented chain of custody.

title: Emerging-Market Multigrade Methods for US Microschools
one_liner: License and adapt proven low-cost, paper-based, self-paced multigrade teaching systems from Colombia, Bangladesh and India, and sell them as a turnkey kit and training to US microschools and shrinking rural districts.
customer: Microschool founders and pod networks, including the roughly 1,000 microschools the brief says are in limbo awaiting federal scholarship-credit rules, paying $1,500-5,000 a year. Homeschool co-ops with ESA money and small rural districts forced into combined-grade classes are the next buyers.
problem: One adult with 6-25 kids across several ages is now the standard microschool model. Guides are often uncredentialed (about two-thirds at Alpha School), 48% of microschool students in one dataset have special needs, and most run on screens. 61% of teachers want less device use, and AI tutors have shown no benefit over plain practice in a two-year Tennessee study.
solution: Sequenced, printable learning guides for K-6 math and literacy, peer-tutoring routines, student-run classroom governance, a 2-day guide training plus six weekly remote coaching calls, and paper mastery checkpoints. The checkpoints double as evidence for scholarship-granting organizations and ESA administrators. Licence terms give originators such as Escuela Nueva (Colombia), BRAC's one-room schools (Bangladesh) or Rishi Valley's School in a Box (India) a royalty share, so the deal funds their work too.
why_now: The federal scholarship tax credit starts in 2027 with 31 states opted in and rules still unwritten, so founders are looking for defensible academics. K-12 enrollment is heading from 49.4M to 46.9M by 2031 and more than 1,000 schools closed this year, so multi-age classes are coming to ordinary rural districts. Screen fatigue, AI bans in NYC and LAUSD, and weak AI-tutor evidence all push buyers toward paper and evidence-backed methods.
revenue_model: A one-time kit plus training at $1,500-3,000 per microschool (about $300 per student), a $600-2,400 annual coaching subscription, and district pilots at $15-40k. Royalties of 10-15% go to the licensors.
non_obvious_insight: The US treats one-adult-many-ages classrooms as a Silicon Valley invention. Countries that built them out of necessity decades ago have field-tested materials that are cheap, paper-based, robust to bad connectivity and teacher-light. Those traits match what US buyers suddenly want in 2026: fewer screens, no AI dependence, and documented outcomes. The emerging-market side is the supplier of know-how, not the customer.
first_30_days: Contact the licensors and negotiate a one-subject pilot licence (grades 2-5 math) in English. Print five paper guide sets. Recruit five microschools through founder communities and networks like the National Microschooling Center at $1,200 each. Record baseline scores with NWEA MAP or i-Ready and re-test after 10 weeks so the results become the first case study.

title: Dead-Zone Analytics to Price Satellite Add-Ons
one_liner: A tool that finds the small share of subscribers who will pay for satellite coverage, and prices it for them.
customer: Regional and mid-size mobile network operators and MVNOs launching satellite-to-phone services.
problem: Satellite-mobile partnerships are multiplying, but 'key questions remain unresolved' (Satellite Today, Sept 2026): carriers do not know how to price or differentiate them, and European operators disagree on their value. Giving the service away destroys value.
solution: Software that runs inside the operator's data environment and computes per-subscriber out-of-coverage dwell time and travel patterns. It segments buyers, runs price and offer experiments, and measures incremental ARPU and churn. It also tells network planners where satellite fills gaps more cheaply than a new site.
why_now: Deals with SpaceX, AST and others are now signed in bulk. Operators need to justify them commercially. SpaceX holds its own spectrum, which raises the stakes for carrier differentiation.
revenue_model: Revenue share of 5-10% of incremental add-on revenue, or a $/subscriber-year fee. Fixed-fee analytics packages for smaller operators.
non_obvious_insight: The value of satellite coverage is concentrated in perhaps 5-10% of subscribers who spend real time outside coverage (rural, hunters, truckers, boaters). Pricing to them beats a blanket giveaway.
first_30_days: Sign one regional operator as a design partner. Run a free 60-day retrospective on anonymized coverage and dwell data, and show the segment size and revenue case. Convert to a pilot on real offers.

title: Paid Holds: Options Market for Booking Agents
one_liner: A merchant plugin that sells time-limited holds on appointments, tables and inventory to shopping and booking agents, so agent traffic becomes fee revenue for the merchant instead of something to block.
customer: Wallet-holding consumer assistant agents and browser agents, which pay through AP2, ACP or Stripe/Tempo MPP rails. Supply side is independent restaurants, salons, dentists, physios, tee-time, boat and experience operators on Acuity, Square Appointments, Booksy, Cal.com or Mindbody.
problem: Agents shop in parallel. One errand fans out to 20-50 merchants and the agent wants to keep the best option open until its principal approves. Free holds are free options, so merchants see phantom demand, no-show slots and sold-out tables. Their response is to block agents: eBay barred buy-for-me agents in Feb 2026 and Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent on 22 Sept 2026.
solution: The merchant sets a hold price (for example 2-5% of ticket value, $1 minimum) and a duration (10 minutes to 24 hours). The agent calls hold(), pays programmatically and gets a signed hold receipt the merchant honors. If the agent converts, the fee is credited to the booking. If not, the merchant keeps it and we take 25%. The service also dedupes so retrying agents don't double-book. Later, hold prices float with demand, giving each slot an implied option value.
why_now: Google's AP2 v0.2 added human-not-present payments and moved to the FIDO Alliance. Stripe and Tempo's Machine Payments Protocol went live in March 2026, and Visa and Mastercard both have agent rails. Merchants are blocking agents right now, and the Ninth Circuit vacated Amazon's injunction against Perplexity in Aug 2026, so blocking is legally shaky. Visa expects millions of agent-made purchases this holiday season.
revenue_model: 25% of hold fees, plus a 1-2% referral fee on converted bookings. The merchant plugin is free to install. Later, a paid demand-analytics dashboard for merchants showing agent search intent by slot.
non_obvious_insight: Merchants are not hostile to agents. They are hostile to free options. Agents are the first buyers rational enough to price optionality, so charging for holds turns an adversarial scraping problem into a market. Airlines already sell fare holds, so the concept is proven with humans. Agents make it viable at $1 scale, and the hold price becomes a demand signal merchants have never had.
first_30_days: Build on the public webhooks and APIs of Cal.com, Acuity and Square Appointments. Recruit about 40 independent salons, barbers and physios in one metro with a free plugin, paying them out of our own test agents' wallets. Ship an MCP server exposing hold_and_book. Get 3 consumer-agent or browser-agent builders to integrate through x402/MPP hackathons. Measure hold-to-book conversion and no-show reduction, then charge live fees in months 2-3.

title: Elder-Intelligible Voice for Healthcare AI Calls
one_liner: An audio layer that reshapes AI-agent voices so listeners 75+ with age-related hearing loss actually understand phone calls, sold per minute to healthcare voice-agent companies.
customer: Healthcare voice-AI vendors, pharmacies, payers and IVR providers whose outbound calls mostly reach people over 70.
problem: Voice agents are being deployed to call seniors about refills, discharge follow-ups and plan outreach. TTS is tuned for young ears, and phone audio cuts off above roughly 3.4 kHz, which is exactly where age-related hearing loss erases consonants (s, f, th, sh). Seniors mishear dates and doses, get frustrated and hang up. The vendor logs it as 'low engagement' and blames the patient.
solution: A drop-in post-processor between the TTS engine and the telephony stream: clear-speech prosody (slower on key phrases, pauses, sharper consonant timing), spectral reshaping tuned to typical presbycusis profiles, and optional per-caller calibration ('say the number you hear'). Add built-in comprehension checks like read-back of the dose. Prove it with a benchmark from a paid panel of 100 older listeners that shows word-recognition gains, then ship it as an API billed per audio minute.
why_now: Healthcare voice agents scaled fast in 2025-26 and their audience is old. Research already shows a clear-speech intelligibility benefit for synthetic voices. Low-latency neural audio processing is now cheap, and no one yet owns the psychoacoustics layer that sits under all those voices.
revenue_model: $0.01-0.03 per audio minute as an add-on, with enterprise minimums of $2-5k/month. Paid listening-panel certification packages (~$15k) that customers can cite in compliance and sales.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats 'voice for older adults' as a warmth and tone problem. It is a psychoacoustics plus telephony-bandwidth problem, and the fix is measurable in word-recognition scores, which makes it sellable. Older listeners can't tell they are the problem, so they just stop answering.
first_30_days: Recruit 30-40 adults 75+ from senior centers, paying $25 for a 40-minute listening test. Build a prototype on open-source TTS plus clear-speech DSP. Publish the intelligibility gain as a 2-page brief. Pitch 15 healthcare voice-agent startups with a free A/B test on 500 calls and aim to sign 2 paid pilots.

title: Code-Upgrade Packages for Home Daycares
one_liner: Fixed-price, state-specific remodel packages plus permit navigation that help licensed in-home daycares climb to the next capacity tier, for example 6 to 12 kids.
customer: Licensed family child care providers (capacity 4-8) who want to add slots. Projects are financed by CDFI or SBA microloans, state facility grants, or employers buying slots under the expanded 45F credit.
problem: Family homes are the fastest-growing licensed supply (+4.3% in 2024) versus +1.5% for centers, but growth stalls at capacity thresholds where code and licensing rules jump (egress, fire separation and alarms, second exit, restroom count, fenced yard). Providers face 3-6 agencies (zoning, building, fire, health, licensing) and small builders do not want $6K jobs. The supply map is measured in licensed slots, so this stall is invisible to policy.
solution: Ship a 'capacity ladder' of productized scopes per state (Step 1: 6 to 8 kids, Step 2: 8 to 12). Each has pre-drawn plans, a vetted small-contractor network on fixed prices, and a navigator who files zoning, building, fire and licensing applications. The provider repays from extra tuition, since two added kids at about $1,100/month each pays back a $20K job in roughly 9 months. A financing partner sits on top.
why_now: The 2026 45F credit (40%, or 50% for small businesses, with third-party and pooled arrangements; verify with tax counsel) gives employers a reason to fund slots. The dependent-care FSA rose to $7,500. Remodeling and HVAC slowdowns leave small shops idle and glad to take standardized sub-$10K work. Childcare costs $13,128 a year per child, so any added slot has an immediate paying buyer.
revenue_model: $299-499 code-gap assessment, 12-15% platform fee on each package (typically $6-20K total), permit-navigation fee, and financing referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Childcare supply is not blocked by demand or by providers' willingness. It is blocked by building-code step functions, which makes it a construction-scoping problem. Each extra licensed slot adds $12-15K a year of revenue at near-zero real-estate cost, far cheaper than the tens of thousands per slot for new center construction.
first_30_days: Pick one state and work through its child-care resource and referral agency to interview 30 providers. Sell 15-20 paid $299 code-gap assessments, catalog the three most common failures, and sign two small contractors to fixed prices. Close the first five packages, using assessment fees to fund the plan sets.

title: Founder File for Under-18 Hustlers
one_liner: A verified business transcript, tax pack and Roth IRA earned-income record for the parents of teens who legally can't hold the seller accounts their income runs through.
customer: Parents of 14 to 17-year-old sellers (eBay, StockX, GOAT, Whatnot, TikTok Shop, Depop, Shopify), high-school entrepreneurship programs (DECA, FBLA, Junior Achievement, NFTE), and college counselors. $12 to $15 per month or $149 per year, or $5 per student through programs.
problem: Most major marketplaces require sellers to be 18, so teens run their business under a parent's ID and account. The income, cost basis and reputation all legally belong to the parent. The parent gets a 1099-K on gross sales with no cost basis, which looks like profit. The kid can't prove any of it on a college application, and nobody is documenting the earned income that would let the family fund a custodial Roth IRA (contribution capped at the lower of earned income or the annual limit, roughly $7,000 to $7,500 per year).
solution: Founder File connects read-only to platform exports, PayPal and Gmail receipts, matches purchases to sales for cost basis, and produces: (1) a signed Business Transcript PDF for Common App activity entries and scholarship applications, (2) a Schedule C-ready summary and quarterly estimates for the parent, reviewed by a partner CPA, (3) an earned-income letter and referral to Fidelity or Schwab custodial Roth accounts, and (4) an '18th birthday migration' kit to move history to the kid's own accounts.
why_now: The 2025 tax law rolled the 1099-K reporting threshold back toward $20,000 and 200 transactions, so many teen sellers land in a confusing gray zone about reporting. College admissions increasingly reward proof of real work as test-optional policies spread and AI-polished essays get discounted. Teen commerce through TikTok Shop, Whatnot and reselling is at its peak, and Gen Alpha hustle culture is pulling younger kids in.
revenue_model: Parent subscription, per-student pricing through school programs, and referral fees from custodial brokerage accounts. Possible upsell: CPA-reviewed tax filing.
non_obvious_insight: Teen resellers are among the most under-documented earned-income earners in the country. Documenting what they already do unlocks tax-free compounding worth thousands per kid and turns a bedroom hobby into an admissions asset. The buyer is the parent, who pays for college advantage without hesitation, while everyone else sells to the kid.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 teen resellers from the Discord servers I am in. Give them free transcripts in return for parent-approved testimonials. Have a CPA friend sign off on a template. Sell a $49 'Transcript plus Roth IRA setup' bundle to their parents, and offer the transcript to 5 college-counseling and 'teen entrepreneur' TikTok creators for an affiliate cut.

title: Help-Desk Reset Firewall for MSPs
one_liner: A plug-in for ConnectWise, Autotask and HaloPSA that makes it impossible for a technician to reset a password or MFA without out-of-band verification and manager approval.
customer: MSPs and outsourced IT help desks serving SMBs, priced per technician.
problem: IT help desks are a named target of voice deepfakes, and one report says over half of CISOs have seen a successful attack. An MSP technician is a single point of compromise for dozens of client tenants, and techs judge identity by voice and by facts attackers already have. SMB clients have no security team to catch it.
solution: A reset gate inside the ticket. MFA resets, password resets and new-device enrollments require verification through a contact and number pulled from the client's HR system or PSA (never from the caller), a manager approval push, a cooling-off delay with notification to the user's existing devices, and risk scoring (new country, odd hours). Evidence is stored for insurer questionnaires.
why_now: Help-desk social engineering drove major 2025 intrusions, voice cloning removes the tell, and insurers now ask about caller verification. Enterprise help-desk verification vendors ignore the MSP channel.
revenue_model: $15-30 per technician per month plus $1 per client user per month.
non_obvious_insight: MSPs are the most leveraged and least-served target. The control is a process lock, not a detector, so it does not decay when deepfakes improve, and insurance-renewal pressure makes it a required purchase.
first_30_days: Build it as a ConnectWise Manage/HaloPSA webhook plus a Teams approval bot. Recruit 10 MSPs from MSP peer groups and forums at $299 per month, and show the insurance-renewal benefit.

title: Private Road Associations in a Box
one_liner: Turn the neighbors' informal, cash-in-a-coffee-can road fund into a recorded, insurable road association with dues, reserves and competitively bid plowing and grading.
customer: Households on private roads and shared driveways (5-60 homes per road). The urgent buyers are the real estate attorneys, title agents and listing agents whose closings stall without an enforceable road maintenance agreement.
problem: Millions of rural households reach their homes by private roads maintained by handshake. One neighbor plows, some chip in, some free-ride. Washouts and disputes are common. Lenders and title insurers often want a recorded, enforceable maintenance agreement, so sales stall. HOA software assumes an incorporated HOA with a manager, not 12 neighbors and a gravel road.
solution: Fixed-fee formation: map who benefits, draft a state-specific maintenance agreement, record it with the county, and set up a simple legal entity or association where state law allows. Then recurring service: ACH dues collection with reminders and lien-based enforcement where allowed, a reserve fund, standing bids from vetted plow, gravel and grading contractors, a photo log of road condition, and storm-damage documentation packages for county or FEMA requests.
why_now: Post-2020 in-migration put many remote workers on rural private roads. Extreme-weather washouts, such as Hurricane Helene's damage to private roads and bridges in western North Carolina in 2024, showed how many neighborhoods have no entity that can pool money or apply for repair aid. Lenders and insurers keep tightening property-access checks. No vertical software serves informal neighbor groups.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,000 formation fee, paid by the neighborhood or by the seller at closing. $12-25 per household per month for dues administration. A disclosed 5-8% procurement fee on managed contractor bids.
non_obvious_insight: The customer with urgency isn't the neighborhood but the closing. A failed sale costs a seller and an agent five figures, so attorneys and agents will send you deals for a flat fee. Recurring revenue then comes from dues float and admin. At 200 associations you are the largest single buyer of plowing and gravel in a region, which gives you procurement leverage no individual road has.
first_30_days: Pick a state dense with private roads (Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, or the North Carolina mountains). Get an attorney to draft a reusable agreement template. Partner with 3-5 real estate attorneys and title agents who see failed closings. Sell a $1,500 'closing rescue' formation package. Run 2 pilot associations with free dues collection for 6 months to prove the workflow.

title: Pickleball Court Noise Pre-Clearance Reports
one_liner: Standardized acoustic siting reports and low-cost monitoring loggers that let HOAs, senior communities and parks approve or defend pickleball courts before neighbors sue.
customer: HOA and condo boards, management companies, 55+ and retirement communities adding courts, city parks departments, and hotels, gyms and churches that want courts. They pay $1,200-$3,500 per site, plus a monthly logger rental. Complainant attorneys are a secondary buyer.
problem: Pickleball's popping sound is a legal flashpoint. In February 2026 two homeowners in Parkside at Boca Trail (203 homes) sued to shut two courts. Testing found up to 73 dB against a 55 dB city nuisance threshold, about 900 pops per hour, and nearest homes only 67-72 feet away versus the 300-500 feet often recommended. The homeowners have spent over $50,000 in legal fees, and the HOA paid $3,800 for an acoustic study. A 2023 survey found only 30% of residents wanted the courts unchanged and 28% wanted them closed. Boards cannot get neutral, standard evidence.
solution: A 'Court Siting Certificate'. It uses a calibrated Class 2 sound-level meter and a fixed protocol (LAmax, LAeq and 1-4 kHz pop-band readings at property lines and the nearest homes), then models the results against that municipality's ordinance. We keep a database of local noise ordinances and hours rules for the fastest-growing pickleball markets. The report ranks mitigation options by dB reduction per dollar: USA Pickleball's Quiet Category paddles and balls, acoustic fencing, hours limits and court orientation. A signed, board-meeting-ready PDF follows. Boards can also rent solar-powered sound loggers at $99/month to produce a continuous dB record for disputes.
why_now: Pickleball searches are about 8.4M (+42%). Glimpse reports retirement homes 'rushing to add the sport' and $10 CPCs. Lawsuits are arriving in 2026, the Boca Raton case being the first of its kind in Palm Beach County, and boards are converting tennis courts (this HOA did so in 2021). Every new court adds exposure.
revenue_model: $1,200-$3,500 per pre-clearance report or dispute audit, $99/month logger rental with monthly compliance reports, and referral fees from acoustic-fence installers and quiet-equipment retailers. Later: annual retainers with HOA management companies covering 50+ communities.
non_obvious_insight: Boards are not really buying noise reduction. They are buying neutral evidence and a defensible process before the fight starts. The Boca Raton case shows the asymmetry: a $3,800 study against $50,000+ in resident legal fees, with a split community (https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/pickleball-noise-sparks-lawsuit-tony-123055657.html). Glimpse's trend data flags pickleball demand among seniors and retirement homes (https://meetglimpse.com/trends/). The popular advice articles offer 'acoustic fencing, sound barriers, landscaping, buffer zones' but no costs, standards or benchmarks (https://spinwavepickleball.com/a/blog/pickleball-noise). A published, comparable measurement standard becomes the reference document that lawyers, city staff and boards all cite.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: buy two Class 2 meters and write the measurement protocol and report template, and compile ordinances for Florida, Arizona, Texas, the Carolinas and California metros. Days 8-20: cold-email 200 HOA management firms and community managers with a $750 pilot audit offer, and publish a 'pickleball noise ordinance by city' page for SEO. Days 21-30: complete 5 audits, get one board to publicly cite the report, and sign an installer referral partnership.

title: Offline Distilled Agent Box for Denied Networks
one_liner: Ruggedized GPU box that runs small models distilled from a unit's own GenAI.mil agents, with zero connectivity.
customer: National Guard and reserve units, Army and Marine tactical staffs, border and disaster-response agencies, and defense integrators serving units in disconnected or denied environments.
problem: GenAI.mil is unclassified only and needs connectivity, yet users built more than 100k custom agents. The CDAO says compute is the binding constraint, and classified models cannot train in commercial data centers. Units in the field cannot use any of it.
solution: A service that takes a unit's approved agent workflows on GenAI.mil, distills them into small open-weight models with tool wrappers, and ships them on a rugged 1-2 GPU box with a one-screen interface. It updates by sneakernet with signed model bundles.
why_now: Open-weight small models are now good enough for narrow tasks. Right-sizing to cut inference cost is an explicit DoD priority, and model-vendor politics make owning a portable, vendor-independent model attractive.
revenue_model: $40-90K per box and $2-5K per month for update and distillation services. Government pilot funding via SBIR or CSO awards.
non_obvious_insight: The 100k user-built agents are an unwritten requirements document for what warfighters want. The winner distills the demand signal, not the model.
first_30_days: Ask 3 Guard units for one repetitive workflow (maintenance triage, reporting). Build a demo on commodity hardware with an open-weight model. Apply for one SBIR topic and ask an integrator for a paid subcontract.

title: Kin Circles: Chosen-Family Covenants for Solo Agers
one_liner: A structured program where 6-8 unrelated adults form a witnessed, legally backed chosen-family circle that covers emergencies, hospital discharge and funerals.
customer: Adults aged 50-75 with no spouse or children (AARP finds about 12% of Americans over 50 age solo, and Census data show 15.2 million adults over 55 are childless), with senior-living operators and hospitals as second-tier buyers.
problem: At crisis moments such as surgery, discharge, dementia and death, solo agers have no designated person who is legally empowered and emotionally committed to show up. Friendships drift because obligations are unspecified, unwitnessed and not legally recognised.
solution: A six-week guided formation of a Kin Circle of 6-8 people. It produces a written covenant of specific mutual obligations (rides after surgery, weekly check-ins, holiday dinners), a legal packet through flat-fee partner attorneys (health-care proxy, HIPAA release, power of attorney, funeral instructions), and a public vow ceremony with witnesses. An annual renewal ritual and a simple escalation ladder (if someone misses two check-ins the circle is pinged) keep it alive.
why_now: Solo aging is a demographic wave: 43% of women aged 75+ live alone, and about 4 in 10 childless older adults live alone. Loneliness is a public-health issue, and 'chosen family' is mainstream. Guardianship abuse headlines have made older adults want plans that keep them out of the court system.
revenue_model: Formation packages of roughly $500-800 per person, membership of about $12 per month, annual renewal rituals at around $150 per circle, and licensing of the program to senior-living operators and hospital discharge teams. Legal work is sold by the attorney at a flat fee, with no fee-splitting.
non_obvious_insight: Marriage works because it bundles vow, witnesses and legal status into an obligation stack, and platonic groups lack all three. Unbundle that stack and rebuild it for a group; six to eight people share the load so no one burns out, unlike a single friend or a single adult child.
first_30_days: Recruit three pilot circles through community centers, Meetup and solo-aging forums. Sign two estate-planning attorneys for a flat-fee legal packet. Host the first witnessed 'vow night' and film it for testimonials.
